evidence.note: semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Salary is a continuous money amount between about 32k and 125k, and the schema requires it to be above 29000. It does not identify anyone, and averages and sums of it make sense. Evidence: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT salary) AS n_distinct, MIN(salary), MAX(salary), AVG(salary) FROM instructor -> [['50', '50', '32241.56', '124651.41', '77600.18819999999']] scale (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Salary is a positive money amount with a true zero, so a ratio like 'the highest salary is about 3.9 times the lowest' makes sense. Evidence: SELECT MIN(salary), MAX(salary), MAX(salary)/MIN(salary) AS max_to_min_ratio FROM instructor -> [['32241.56', '124651.41', '3.8661717981387995']] unit (adaptation, 2026-09-30): The values are numeric(8,2) money amounts with two decimal places, in the same currency convention as department.budget (catalogued as USD). Evidence: SELECT salary FROM instructor ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 5 -> [['124651.41'], ['121141.99'], ['119921.41'], ['118143.98'], ['117836.5']] additive (adaptation, 2026-09-30): Each instructor row has one salary, so adding salaries across instructors gives a department's salary total. Evidence: SELECT dept_name, COUNT(*) AS instructors, SUM(salary) AS payroll FROM instructor GROUP BY dept_name ORDER BY payroll DESC -> [['Statistics', '6', '406772.64999999997'], ['Athletics', '5', '385490.99'], ['Cybernetics', '4', '385386.27'], ['Marketing', '4', '336389.75'], ['Pol. Sci.', '3', '300159.22'], ['Elec. Eng.', '4', '296650.95999999996']]

semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): 50 instructors fall into 17 departments, with several instructors per department. It is a grouping label, not a unique key on this table. Evidence: SELECT dept_name, COUNT(*) AS instructors FROM instructor GROUP BY dept_name ORDER BY instructors DESC -> [['Statistics', '6'], ['Athletics', '5'], ['Marketing', '4'], ['English', '4'], ['Elec. Eng.', '4'], ['Cybernetics', '4']]

semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): 2000 students fall into 20 departments, about 100 per department, so the column groups rows. Evidence: SELECT dept_name, COUNT(*) AS students, AVG(tot_cred) AS avg_tot_cred FROM student GROUP BY dept_name ORDER BY students DESC -> [['Civil Eng.', '120', '63.94166666666667'], ['Languages', '119', '60.6890756302521'], ['History', '117', '71.68376068376068'], ['Pol. Sci.', '109', '64.88990825688073'], ['Comp. Sci.', '108', '65.72222222222223'], ['Astronomy', '106', '67.36792452830188']]

semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): 200 courses fall into 20 departments, about 10 per department, so the column groups rows. Evidence: SELECT dept_name, COUNT(*) AS courses, SUM(credits) AS total_credits FROM course GROUP BY dept_name ORDER BY courses DESC -> [['Cybernetics', '20', '67'], ['Finance', '14', '49'], ['Psychology', '13', '44'], ['Mech. Eng.', '12', '40'], ['Accounting', '12', '40'], ['Physics', '10', '38']]

semantic_role (adaptation, 2026-09-30): About 9 distinct letter grades (A through C-) split the 30000 enrolments into sizeable groups. The scale should stay ordinal, since the grades are ordered. Evidence: SELECT grade, COUNT(*) AS enrolments FROM takes GROUP BY grade ORDER BY grade -> [['A ', '3318'], ['A+', '3318'], ['A-', '3268'], ['B ', '3334'], ['B+', '3355'], ['B-', '3411']]
